text:
alice_support: Hey — acme is hitting failures on their Private/VPC deploy: model pulls and package installs fail with TLS verify errors. They asked for a minimal egress allowlist (hosts + ports) and any cert/OCSP endpoints we need to mention. Can eng confirm the canonical hostnames and any IP guidance?

acme_devops: Throwing logs here — deploy pod fails when curling the registry: 
```
$ curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.ai/api/v1/models
*   Trying 52.85.61.12:443...
* Connected to model-registry.redwood.ai (52.85.61.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ...
* server certificate verification failed. CAfile: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt CRLfile: none
* SSL: certificate subject name (CN=cloudflare) does not match target host name 'model-registry.redwood.ai'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name (CN=cloudflare) does not match target host name 'model-registry.redwood.ai'
```
Also seeing a lot of OCSP timeouts when apt/yum tries to fetch packages (apt-get update stalls).

alice_support: Thanks — two asks: 1) definitive list of FQDNs and ports to allow for model registry, telemetry, auth, package pulls; 2) advice for customers that can only allow IP/CIDR (we prefer allowing by hostname/SNI).

rob_sre: Short answer: allow outbound TLS (443) to the following hostnames (these are what our runtime and installer call out). If you must allow IPs, see note after the host list — most are fronted by CDNs so IPs are dynamic.

- model-registry.redwood.ai
- api.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai (OAuth/JWK endpoints)
- telemetry.redwood.ai and telemetry-cdn.redwood.ai
- artifacts.redwoodmodels.s3.amazonaws.com (model artifacts stored in S3)
- models-cdn.redwood.ai (CDN for model shards)
- configs.redwood.ai (config & rollout fetches)
- cdn.jsdelivr.net (used by some quickstarts)
- pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org (pip packages)
- registry-1.docker.io and auth.docker.io (container pulls when using Docker-based installers)
- security.ubuntu.com and archive.ubuntu.com (apt packages during image build)

All traffic is TLS (port 443). Some fallbacks use HTTP (80) but we recommend only opening 443 and letting TLS handle redirects.

maya_engineer: Additional notes on TLS/OCSP/certs:
- We use public certs (Let’s Encrypt / Cloudflare fronted). The cert presented may be from our CDN, so SNI must be preserved — allow outbound SNI for the hostname.
- OCSP/CRL checks happen to the CA OCSP endpoints. If your proxy blocks OCSP, you will see apt/apt-get stalls and TLS verify failures. Common OCSP hosts you may need to allow: `ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org`, `ocsp.digicert.com`, `ocsp.pki.goog` (depending on CA).
- Avoid TLS interception that replaces cert chains; this breaks cert pinning and JWK discovery for auth. If you must MITM TLS, make sure the proxy injects a trusted CA into the nodes and supports SNI passthrough for host-based matches.

acme_devops: fwiw we do have a corporate proxy that intercepts TLS and adds a custom CA. Could that explain the CN mismatch?

maya_engineer: Yes — that explains the CN mismatch. The fix is either: 1) configure the proxy to allow passthrough for the Redwood hostnames (no MITM), or 2) install the proxy's root CA into the OS-level trust store on the nodes that run the installer & runtime, and ensure the CA is trusted by curl/apt/openssl.

rob_sre: If you absolutely can only allow by IP/CIDR, note that most of the above hostnames are behind CDNs (CloudFront/Cloudflare) so IPs can change. Suggested approach:
- Allow the AWS CloudFront and S3 IP ranges (from the official AWS ip-ranges.json) for the region(s) your deployment uses. Example commonly used prefixes (not exhaustive): `13.32.0.0/14`, `13.54.63.0/24`, `52.46.0.0/15`, `52.95.245.0/24`.
- Allow Cloudflare IPs if you are seeing Cloudflare in the cert chain. Example Cloudflare prefixes: `104.16.0.0/12`, `162.158.0.0/15`, `141.101.64.0/18`.
- If you allow by CIDR, keep a job that refreshes AWS/Cloudflare IP lists weekly — the services rotate ranges.

alice_support: Quick troubleshooting commands to run so we can validate from your side:
```
# check TLS + SNI chain
$ openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai -showcerts

# verbose curl to see where verification fails
$ curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.ai/api/v1/health

# test pip reachability
$ python -m pip install --no-cache-dir -vv somepackage
```

acme_devops: Running openssl now, getting similar mismatch. We'll try adding the proxy CA to the node truststore and report back. Also please confirm ports: just 443 outbound or any others?

maya_engineer: Primarily 443. For package downloads some tooling hits 80 for redirects but TLS endpoints are the canonical ones. If the installer uses metadata services to fetch instance metadata in cloud images (not in private onprem), that uses 169.254.169.254 (local) — not relevant for private installs.

egress-bot: Automated note: If you need an official KB, see https://kb.redwood.ai/egress-private for the canonical allowlist and periodic IP lists (we update weekly).

alice_support: Thanks — acme, please try the two options (SNI passthrough or install proxy CA). If that doesn't work, reply here with the output of the openssl/curl commands and we'll loop in eng infra with a packet capture request.

acme_devops: Will do. Appreciate the quick triage.

rob_sre: One last tip — if you see OCSP timeouts specifically from apt, test allowing outbound TCP to the OCSP host (port 80/443 depending on CA) and re-run `apt-get update` with `-o Acquire::http::Timeout=60` to surface the failures quicker.

alice_support: marking this thread for follow-up tomorrow. If acme posts results we'll continue here and escalate to eng-infra if needed.
